title: Tunnels & Vehicle Fires
whatItIs: In a tunnel there is little room and little light. A breakdown or a fire there needs quick, calm action.
keyFacts: Before a tunnel: dipped headlights on, sunglasses off, and tune in to the radio for traffic information.
Keep at least a two-second gap in a tunnel.
Broken down in a tunnel: hazard lights on, engine off, get out and call for help from an emergency point.
Fire in a tunnel: drive out if you can. If not, stop, engine off, leave the keys in and get out at once.
Engine fire anywhere: get everyone out to a safe place and call 999. Don't open the bonnet.

visual.caption: If your car catches fire in a tunnel

items.title: Drive out
items.text: If the car still drives, keep going and leave the tunnel.

items.title: Can't drive out?
items.text: Pull over, hazard lights on, switch off the engine.

items.title: Keys in, get out
items.text: Leave the keys so the car can be moved. Get everyone out.

items.title: Raise the alarm
items.text: Use an emergency point. Use an extinguisher only if it is safe.

items.title: Head for an exit
items.text: Walk to the nearest emergency exit straight away.

a.label: Breakdown in a tunnel
points: Get out, call from an emergency point

b.label: Fire in a tunnel
points: If not: keys in, get out at once

onTheTest.question: Your car catches fire in a tunnel, but you can still drive it. What should you do?
options: Stop at once and get out
onTheTest.why: If you can, drive out of the tunnel. If you can't, pull over, switch off the engine, leave the keys in and get out.

traps: Leave the keys in: it lets the emergency services move your car.
Opening the bonnet on an engine fire lets in air and makes it worse.
Take off your sunglasses before the tunnel: it is darker inside.
